D007-D015_h020.question:
I’ve just felt worn down for almost a year now. Since my wife died, it’s like a gray film over everything. I used to like working in the garden and playing cards at the seniors’ center, but I don’t get any enjoyment out of those anymore, so I mostly stay home. I’m sad most days, just this heavy feeling, and I’m tired all the time, even if I’ve done almost nothing.

My appetite’s gone way down; I pick at my food and sometimes just have toast for dinner. Sleep is broken. I fall asleep okay, but then I’m up two or three times a night and lie there for an hour, exhausted but unable to drift off again.

The last several months, maybe eight or so, I’ve started to feel like something terrible is coming. I keep thinking the world is on the brink of some kind of collapse, like there’s no point in planning for anything. I can’t shake that thought. Sometimes, usually in the evenings, I smell this strange, rotten sort of odor in the house that no one else notices. It makes me even more uneasy. All of this has made it hard to manage the house or keep up with friends.
D007-D015_h020.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D007-D015_h020.answer: A & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h021.question:
It’s hard to explain without sounding strange. For almost a year and a half now, it’s like my life split in two. On one side I’m this burned‑out programmer who mostly lies in bed. I can sleep 12–14 hours and still feel exhausted. When I’m awake, I just stare at the screen. I’ve stopped working on personal projects, stopped going out with friends. I know I should shower, answer emails, clean up, but I just…don’t start. It feels like the drive is gone.

At the same time, I feel weirdly empty. Not sad exactly—more like everything is on mute. My body, though, won’t sit still some days: I pace laps in my apartment, tap my fingers, rub my hands together until the skin’s raw, like I’m wired and numb at the same time.

Then there are episodes where I’m convinced I’m different—like I’m meant to create some breakthrough code that’ll change the world, or that people are watching me because of it. Sometimes I see shapes or figures in the room, like someone standing in the corner. Other times I’ll get stuck talking in rhymes—“time, crime, sublime”—and it just pours out until it sounds like nonsense. There are also stretches where I basically shut down, barely moving or responding, just sitting there while everything goes on around me. All of this has been going on for about a year and a half, maybe a bit longer.
D007-D015_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h021.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h022.question:
I’ve been working at City Hall for over twenty years, so I’m used to routine, but for about a year and a half everything’s felt…hollow. It’s like there’s nothing inside, just this blankness. Things I used to enjoy—watching football with my kids, weekend barbecues—feel like chores now. I go through the motions, but I don’t get anything out of it.

My wife says I move and talk slower. Even walking from my car to the office feels like wading through water. At my desk I’ll just stare at a file, and when someone asks me a simple question, I catch myself drifting off onto other topics and never really answering what they asked. Colleagues sometimes look confused, and I only realize afterward that I’ve gone off track.

At home, I’ve become suspicious. I keep thinking my wife is seeing someone else. There’s no real proof, but little things—her phone lighting up, her getting home late—feel like “signs” I can’t shake off, no matter how much she explains.

Sleep is bad. For around the same time, about a year and a half, I’ve had these awful, vivid dreams where something is crawling on me or grabbing me, and sometimes when I’m awake I still feel things brushing against my skin when nothing’s there. I wake up drenched in sweat, heart pounding, but even then I don’t really feel scared—just empty and exhausted. It’s gotten hard to keep up with work and family because of all this.
D007-D015_h022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h022.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h023.question:
It’s been… about a year and a half, maybe a bit more, since I’ve really felt like myself. On air I can still read the prompter, but off camera I barely talk. My producers say I’ve become “quiet,” but it’s more like there’s nothing inside to say. I feel flat, like I’m watching my life instead of living it.

Sleep is a mess. I fall asleep, then wake up at two or three, just staring at the ceiling for an hour or more, then dozing, then waking again. By morning I’m exhausted, and when people ask me simple questions, it takes forever to answer. Even my own voice sounds slow, dragged out.

For about the last year and a half, I’ve been completely sure that one of the senior executives at the network is secretly in love with me. There are “signs” in how he looks into the camera during internal calls, or which stories I’m assigned. I know everyone says it’s just work, but I feel it’s more.

Sometimes, when I’m alone, I feel fingers brushing my arms or someone pressing lightly on my back, but no one’s there. And when I try to explain all of this, the words get tangled and come out wrong, so I just… stop talking. I kind of freeze up, even my body feels like it can be put in a position and I’ll just stay there. It’s been ruining my work and my social life, but I can’t quite explain how it all fits together.
D007-D015_h023.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h023.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h024.question:
I guess it really started about a year and a half ago. I’ve just felt low most days, like there’s this weight on me I can’t shake. I used to like working on cars, staying late at the shop, joking with the guys, going fishing on weekends. Now none of that really feels like anything. I go through the motions, but I don’t get that spark.

I sleep enough hours, my wife says even more than before, but I wake up feeling like I barely slept. Getting out of bed feels like wading through mud. Even at work, I move slower, customers notice I take longer to do simple stuff, like just walking over to get a tool.

Sometimes, when I’m under a car or just zoning out, I smell this weird perfume or flowers, really strong, and no one else smells it. That’s around the same time I started thinking this woman who comes into the shop sometimes… I’m pretty sure she’s into me, like she’s sending me signals, even though I know I’m married and she barely talks to me. I’ll start telling my wife about it and then I end up talking about something random, like engines from the ’90s, and forget what I was saying.

She gets mad because I’ll suddenly joke around or make dumb voices with the kids at totally wrong times, like when she’s trying to have a serious talk and I just start goofing off. I know it seems childish, but it sort of pops out. All of this has been messing with my work and home life for over a year now, and I just feel stuck in it.
D007-D015_h024.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h024.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling really low for about a year and a half now. It’s not just “bad days”; it’s like this heavy sadness that doesn’t really lift. I move slower, even walking from my car to the office feels like I’m wading through mud. My husband says I seem “slowed down,” and I can see it in how long it takes me to get simple things done, like loading the dishwasher.  

Sleep is a mess. I fall asleep okay, but I wake up two, three times a night and then lie there for ages, staring at the ceiling, dreading the next workday. It’s affecting my work as an accountant; I’ve started making little mistakes in spreadsheets I never would’ve made before.

There’s something else that’s harder to explain. For the past year and a half or so, I’ve been convinced that a senior manager at a client firm has feelings for me. He doesn’t say anything outright, but I feel it in how he looks at me, certain emails, small things. My family says I’m reading too much into it, but it feels very real.

Sometimes, especially in the evening, I feel like something is lightly brushing my skin or crawling on my arms when nothing’s there. And when I talk about all this, my thoughts jump around—I catch myself starting on one thing and drifting off to something else. My husband also says I talk a lot less than I used to, like getting words out is an effort. Occasionally I’ll sit or hold my body in a certain way and just stay like that without really thinking about it, until someone points it out.
D007-D015_h025.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D007-D015_h025.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
